governance.attested_by: ercot82 measured-rtolcap, session 2026-07-18 (ERCOT handoff Lane 2 — the ercot-82 measured-RTOLCAP vs forward-formula supply-cap A/B). REGISTERED CANDIDATE (keeper swap owner-only). The 2026-07-18-ercot81-nonreleasable-as keeper recipe with ONE corrected input: ercot_reserve_supply_forward=false, so the ERCOT multi-product co-opt's reserve-supply cap is sourced from the MEASURED ercot_<year>_ordc_reserves_hourly.parquet RTOLCAP/RTOFFCAP series (the on-line responsive reserve capability ERCOT published) instead of the WS-A forward formula. This closes the surfaced prb_overrides stomp: the keeper recipe's coal_prb_sigmoid_overrides carried ercot_reserve_supply_forward=true, which run_year applies last and stomped the meta top-level false (ERCOT-65 defect class), so every ercot76..81 keeper had silently solved on the forward-formula cap (mean 16.1 GW) rather than the measured parquet the recipe documentation and scarcity.py docstring claim ('backcast with ercot_reserve_supply_forward off returns the MEASURED series byte-identical (the validation target)'). Both channels now resolve false, so the recipe is internally consistent and reads the measured series. Zero fitted scalars: the only change is measured-vs-formula input selection, which per CLAUDE.md rule 14 must prefer the measured series in backcast unless adjudicated misaligned; it is not misaligned (it is the exact published series the co-opt cap was designed to read in backcast).
governance.note: Single-delta A/B against the ercot81 keeper (full-span 2023+2024+2025 one invocation, same machine, rule 16). The measured cap is dispatch-INERT outside already-formed tight hours and marginally toward-actual in the chartered 2023: C3a-2023 -22.1% -> -21.8% (model 49.94 -> 50.14 vs RT 64.12), C3b-2023 NRMSE 0.456 -> 0.449, C3c-2023 >$200 57 -> 58 h (RT 181); 2024 and 2025 dispatch-IDENTICAL (C3a +2.1% / -3.4%, C3b 0.303 / 0.086, C3c 22 / 0 all unchanged). Guards all HELD: Aug-2023 monthly residual -64.9 -> -63.1 (model 126.8 -> 128.6 vs RT 191.7), Jun/Sep-2023 residuals UNCHANGED at -12.1 / -22.1 (no ERCOT-78/79 over-shoot re-inflation), false-positive >$200 count UNCHANGED at 8 h, 2023 deep tail 57/54/38 -> 58/55/39 (toward actual 181/104/61). Measured RTOLCAP annual-mean spinning tier 13.5 GW vs the forward formula's 16.1 GW; the two differ mainly in the tight tail hours the LP was already pricing, where the lower measured cap adds a hair more tightness. Same fail set and NOT-YET determination as the keeper; the remaining Aug-2023 mid-band ($200-1000, model $59-104 at measured RTOLCAP p50 ~7.9 GW) is the ledgered ERCOT-75/77 offer-formation family, out of scope for the reserve-supply cap (rule 13).

exceptions.magnitude: 57h vs RT actual 181h (0.31x, FAIL — rubric v2.7 RT basis); 2024 22h vs 53 (0.42x FAIL); 2025 0h vs 31 (0.00x FAIL)
exceptions.reason: SCARCITY-TAIL COLLAPSE ON THE UNIT-ONLY AVAILABILITY ENVELOPE (ERCOT-80). Same structural finding as ERCOT-79: the deposed ercot76 keeper caught the real scarcity tail (2023 179h vs 181) on PHANTOM fleet tightness manufactured by the CAMPD facility-outage detector (daily-cycling CC folded into summer-long false outages). The outage-detection consolidation (PR #2415) deletes the facility layer entirely and makes the per-unit event-based detector the sole outage layer (measured CEMS + EIA-930, no residual), removing the phantom more completely; the tail stays collapsed (57h vs 181; on the real August/summer scarcity hours the model settlement price falls far short). One availability mechanism owned BOTH the Jun/Sep shoulder over-shoot (fixed at ercot79) and the caught tail (un-caught). This is out-of-admissible-representation for the CURRENT offer/scarcity calibration, which was fitted against the phantom-tightened fleet; it is NOT a single-lane mechanism gap. Successor lane: re-calibrate the ERCOT offer curves + ORDC/co-opt against the corrected availability envelope so the real scarcity re-forms on real fleet tightness. Until then ERCOT is NOT-YET.
